title: Tuna & White Bean Salad
description: A fast no-cook lunch with tuna, white beans, lemon, and a little crunch.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use mayonnaise instead of olive oil for a creamier version.

steps.text: Combine tuna, white beans, and optional celery or cucumber in a bowl.
Add olive oil, lemon juice, and black pepper.
Stir gently and serve on toast, crackers, lettuce, or by itself.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 can drained tuna, 1 can white beans, and 1/4 cup chopped celery or cucumber if using.
Add 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Stir gently and serve on toast, crackers, lettuce, or by itself.

storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days.

title: Apple Peanut Butter Oatmeal
description: Warm oatmeal with tender apple and a swirl of peanut butter.
substitutions: Use another nut or seed butter.

steps.text: Combine oats, milk or water, diced apple, and cinnamon in a small saucepan.
Simmer 5–7 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the apple is tender.
Stir in peanut butter and optional sweetener.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1/2 cup oats, 1 cup milk or water, 1/2 diced apple, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon in a small saucepan.
Simmer 5–7 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the apple is tender.
Stir in 1 tablespoon peanut butter and 1 teaspoon brown sugar or maple syrup if using.

storage: Best fresh; refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat with extra liquid.

title: Small-Batch Banana Oat Cookies
description: Soft little cookies made from ripe banana and oats with optional add-ins.
substitutions: Use quick oats for a softer texture.
Skip all add-ins for a two-ingredient version.

steps.text: Heat oven to 350°F and line a small sheet pan.
Mash banana very smooth, then stir in oats and optional cinnamon and add-ins.
Scoop 6 mounds, flatten slightly, and bake 13–15 minutes until set and lightly browned.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 350°F and line a small sheet pan.
Mash 1 ripe banana very smooth. Stir in 1 cup oats plus 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon and 2 tablespoons chocolate chips or raisins if using.
Scoop 6 mounds, flatten slightly, and bake 13–15 minutes until set and lightly browned.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature 1 day or refrigerate up to 4 days.

title: Quick Creamy Polenta Bowls
description: Creamy cornmeal topped simply with cheese, beans, or leftover vegetables.
substitutions: Use regular cornmeal; cook longer as package directs.

steps.text: Bring water or broth to a boil.
Whisk in polenta slowly and cook, stirring often, until thick and tender.
Stir in butter and cheese. Spoon into bowls and top with beans or leftover vegetables if using.

cookSteps.text: Bring 4 cups water or broth to a boil.
Slowly whisk in 1 cup quick-cooking polenta and cook, stirring often, about 10 minutes until thick and tender.
Stir in 1 tablespoon butter and 1/2 cup cheese. Spoon into bowls and top with 1 cup beans or leftover vegetables if using.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat with extra water or milk.
